A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same two-stage acceleration framework, renamed from OUSAC to RSTR, with matching authors and core experiments. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original image-generation experiments on DiT-XL/2, PixArt-alpha, and FLUX, including benchmark results, ablations, robustness tests, and optimization measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds Qwen-Image evaluations, guidance analyses, and cross-model-size and cross-sampler transfer results.

M1.justification: The evolutionary quality-and-sparsity search and region-adaptive SVD calibration optimized by coordinate descent remain intact. Changing the stated no-guidance weight from zero to one aligns the description with the conditional-only prediction rule already present in v1. Additional cache-interval details do not establish a new algorithm.

E1.justification: V2 adds GenEval2 evaluation for text-to-image generation while retaining ImageNet, MSCOCO, PartiPrompts, DrawBench, and GenEval. Qwen-Image and smaller DiT variants primarily expand model configurations within the existing generation tasks.

E2.justification: V2 adds ICC and Adaptive Guidance to the FLUX comparison in Table 3, but removes v1's separate DiT comparison against Adaptive Guidance. Figure 2 replaces conditional-only and random-sparse controls with fixed-interval and time-varying guidance strategies. The new cross-sampler experiment also evaluates an SA-Solver baseline.

E3.justification: V2 reports seven rather than four calibration regions for DiT and PixArt, calibration sets of 50,000/30,000 rather than 10,000/5,000 images, and PixArt search resolution of 256 rather than 128. It introduces Qwen-Image settings, Soft-TIFA AM/GM metrics, and controlled model-size and sampler-transfer protocols. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish which retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds guidance-density, position-shifting, and step-removal ablations; trajectory-curvature and direction analyses; cross-size and cross-sampler transfer; and Qwen threshold and maximum-scale sensitivity tests. It also adds block-error comparisons with rank 1024. V1's 256-resolution DiT rank-allocation table is removed, while reference-length, quantization, and several guidance-strength analyses are retained or relocated.

E5.justification: V2 newly acknowledges variation across optimization runs in Remark A.4 and displays error bars and a shaded active-step range in Figure 9. However, it provides neither run counts or seeds nor an explanation of how those ranges were estimated. This adds limited variability reporting without establishing increased replication.

E6.justification: V2 adds Qwen-Image, transfer, sensitivity, and geometric results. Most main DiT and PixArt scores remain unchanged, but the cached FLUX row changes from 216.48 to 190.36T MACs and from 66.77 to 66.47 GenEval; these are revised reported results, not an established same-setting improvement. DiT TaylorSeer latency changes from 12.08 to 12.79 seconds. Several detailed FLUX category scores and v1's 256-resolution rank-ablation results disappear.

T1.justification: New Appendix A defines guidance-schedule spaces, states and proves a strict-inclusion proposition, and derives an optimal-loss corollary. V1 contains no corresponding formal search-space analysis. The earlier denoising-deviation derivations are retained in Appendix B.1. The new inclusion statement omits common upper bounds needed for the comparator spaces to fit inside the bounded RSTR space.

C1.justification: The principal two-stage acceleration contribution remains. V2 adds an explicit contribution concerning sparse high-scale guidance, coupled position and scale, and indispensable guidance steps. It extends headline claims to Qwen-Image and changes the advertised DiT compute savings from 53% to 57%, although the principal DiT quality results remain unchanged.

C2.justification: V2 introduces substantive explanations connecting effective guidance to low-curvature trajectories and distinct guidance-direction groups, alongside position-scale coupling. It revises interpretations of block sensitivity and region count. New technical limitations acknowledge model/sampler specificity, sequential rather than joint optimization, and incomplete characterization across prompt domains and model families.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds explicit guidance bounds and thresholds, FLUX model/sampler identification, and Qwen-specific configurations; Appendix D elaborates cache intervals and supplies a code-repository link. Conversely, v1's detailed per-model optimization-cost Tables 13–14 and its L2C/HarmoniCa reimplementation disclosure are removed. Repository contents cannot replace the missing local evidence.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for Qwen-Image, GenEval2, T-Stitch, SA-Solver, and several medical-imaging and language-model topics. It elaborates the relationship to interval guidance and weight schedulers while retaining the central positioning around jointly optimizing guidance and caching. Numerous publication and bibliography updates concern already-cited works.

P1.justification: Beyond renaming the paper and method, v2 substantially rewrites the abstract and introduction around spatiotemporal redundancy, reorganizes the method sections, and restructures the experimental narrative. The appendix is reorganized into Sections A–F with a contents page, and several existing analyses move into the main text.

P2.justification: The main text switches to a compact two-column layout. V2 replaces the opening illustration, redraws the synthetic comparison, merges the FLUX benchmark tables, reorganizes block-error plots, and adds several analytical displays. Existing qualitative grids are resized or recombined, and retained tables are relocated or redisplayed.

improvement.justification: Qwen-Image evaluation and controlled transfer and guidance-position tests strengthen evidence for generality and mechanism, while additional limitations clarify applicability. These gains are tempered by removing self-contained optimization-cost tables, the incomplete assumptions in Appendix A's inclusion claim, and reporting inconsistencies: Section 5.2 calls 56.73 to 16.62 seconds a 4.7-fold speedup, although it is approximately 3.41-fold. The net quality improvement is useful but limited.
